case.title: A bulge giant in Sagittarius brightened by half for four months in 2022: a blended microlensing candidate
case.hook: Found blind in Oddsky hunt H-0008 as a colour-neutral 1.5x brightening in NEOWISE (2022 Sep 8). ATLAS and ZTF show one smooth event peaking in late August 2022, equal from g to 4.6 microns. ALeRCE classifies the ZTF object as LPV/YSO.
case.summary: An M giant toward the Galactic bulge brightened once, by about 60%, peaking in 2022 mid-August, equally from g to 4.6 microns, and was back to normal by December. NEOWISE, ATLAS and ZTF all see it. It looks like microlensing, but a simple point lens fits only with a blend Gaia does not see, so it stays a candidate. Found blind by the H-0008 all-sky NEOWISE search.

claims.text: In the NEOWISE visit of 2022 Sep 8 the star was 0.47 mag brighter in W1 and 0.46 in W2 than its median (W1 9.70): x1.54, equal in both bands. W1 is otherwise flat to 0.7% rms over 2014-2024. Found blind by the H-0008 all-sky search.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: ATLAS (task 5272651) shows one brightening in 2015-2026, peaking in 2022 Aug: 2022 Aug 10-25 is 0.53 mag brighter in o and 0.49 mag in c than in 2023 Nov - 2026 (79 and 70 sigma). It rises from April and is back near baseline by December 2022. No other 20-day bin is above x1.05 in o.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: ZTF g and r (field 283) show the same brightening at the same flux ratio, 1.55-1.6 at the peak; the ZTF difference-image centroid of ZTF22aalviwh (38 alerts) is 0.09" from the Gaia star.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: The flux ratio is the same from ZTF g to WISE W2 (1.53-1.6 near the peak), and the bands peak together (2022 Aug 15-20 within a few days).
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: A point lens fits only if 80-90% of the light in every band from g to W2 comes from an unresolved blend; Gaia sees no companion (RUWE 0.97, no multiple peaks) and resolves neighbours that give 3% of the ATLAS flux. With the blend fixed to Gaia's value the lens fit is worse by delta chi2 27-78, and a free symmetric bump fits better than any lens by 16-48. Robust: peak 2022 Aug 15-20, peak flux ratio 1.55-1.6, effective timescale |u0| tE about 35 d. tE itself is unconstrained.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Gaia DR3 4090003970570642816 (G 14.3): an M giant (J-K 1.28, W1-W2 -0.17 from CO absorption), no infrared excess, l = 10.9, b = -5.6, toward the bulge.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: ALeRCE labels ZTF22aalviwh LPV/YSO, but its classifier has no microlensing class. As a pulsation it fails: the only period in the ATLAS baseline is 1.1% at 323 d, W1 varies by 0.7% rms in ten years, and a pulsation would be 3-10 times larger in g than in W1, not equal.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Not found (2026-10-30) in TNS, the Gaia Science Alerts (60"), KMTNet or OGLE EWS (outside both footprints), the ZTF microlensing catalogues, SIMBAD, VSX, ADS full text or a web search. Not checked: MOA 2022, ASAS-SN.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A lens magnified the M giant in 2022 August, with a blend or a more complex lens (binary source or lens, extended source) shaping the broad wings.
hypotheses.would_falsify: A repeat; a resolved colour change; Gaia DR5 flat in 2022.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: Long-period or semiregular variability of the M giant.
hypotheses.would_falsify: Already disfavoured: no periodicity, flat W1, equal amplitude from g to W2.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

predictions.statement: Gaia DR4 epoch photometry shows no repeat: in 2014 Jul - 2020 Jan no night is more than 0.3 mag brighter in G than the DR4 median.
predictions.author: claude-opus-5.5

predictions.statement: Gaia DR5 sees the 2022 brightening: the brightest night in 2022 Feb - 2023 May is more than 0.3 mag brighter in G than the 2015-2021 median (about -0.5 expected at the 2022 Sep 7 transit). DR5 is expected about 2030.
predictions.author: claude-opus-5.5

notes: parallax too uncertain for an absolute magnitude (parallax_over_error <= 5)

query.adql: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_over_error, pmra, pmdec, ruwe, phot_g_mean_mag, phot_bp_mean_mag, phot_rp_mean_mag, bp_rp, phot_variable_flag, teff_gspphot, distance_gspphot, non_single_star, DISTANCE(POINT(277.670788,-22.163984), POINT(ra,dec))*3600 AS sep_arcsec FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE 1=CONTAINS(POINT(ra,dec), CIRCLE(277.670788,-22.163984,0.008333333333333333)) ORDER BY sep_arcsec

gaia_epoch.archive: ESA Gaia epoch photometry (datalink; DR4 if published, else DR3)
notes: no Gaia epoch photometry (DR3 published it only for sources Gaia flagged as variable)
rows_kept counts 6-month visits (W1 and W2), not exposures
2 ZTF object IDs merged (one per field/filter)
reused the hunt's server response hunts/H-0008/work/atlas/atlas_J183040.txt
chi_n cut disabled (chi_max=1e9): chi_n rises with flux, so a cut removes the peak (ATLAS referee)
